raw_response:
I am 64 this year, and I have worked these 13.5 mu in Quzhou for 45 years. I finished middle school, so I can read the numbers on fertilizer bags, and I talk to the seed dealer when I go to town. But mostly I watch what works on my own land and copy the good farmers around me. My son is working in Shijiazhuang, so at home it is just me and my wife. We have a well for water. I keep 8 mu for wheat and then maize, and 5.5 mu for cotton. Cotton brings cash, but it needs too much hand work, so with only two of us I cannot plant more. I may hire two women from the village to help pick cotton in October if the bolls set heavy, but that comes out of the same pocket as fertilizer, so I watch every yuan.

For the 8 mu of winter wheat: Last year I put one 50 kg bag of 16-16-16 compound fertilizer per mu as base, and I will do the same again this year. That is 8 kg of nitrogen, 8 kg of phosphorus, and 8 kg of potassium from that bag. When the wheat turns green in spring, I will spread 20 kg of urea per mu on top, which is about 9 kg more nitrogen. So all together that is 17 kg nitrogen, 8 kg phosphorus, and 8 kg potassium per mu. I will rotary till before I plant. I sow an improved Jimai wheat seed, about 12.5 kg per mu. I will water three times: once when the wheat wakes up, once at jointing, and once when the grain is filling. I spray pesticide twice, once for aphids and once for the leaf disease that comes when it gets damp. I expect about 500 kg per mu. Fertilizer is expensive now, but a bad harvest is worse. I would rather spend an extra 100 yuan on urea than lose yield.

For the summer maize on the same 8 mu: Right after we cut the wheat in June, I plant hybrid maize seed straight into the wheat stubble. No-tillage, because we have no time to waste in June—the season is short. I put 2.5 kg of hybrid seed per mu. At planting I spread 50 kg of compound fertilizer 20-10-10 per mu, which gives 10 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, and 5 kg potassium. When the plants are knee-high, I topdress with 15 kg urea per mu, about 7 kg more nitrogen. Total is about 17 kg nitrogen, 5 kg phosphorus, 5 kg potassium per mu. I will irrigate twice if the rain does not come—once when the tassels show and once during grain filling. Two pesticide sprays are enough for the worms. I expect 550 kg per mu.

For the 5.5 mu of cotton: I plant improved Bt cotton, 1.5 kg seed per mu. In spring I plough deep because cotton roots need loose soil. The base fertilizer is one 50 kg bag of 15-15-15 compound per mu—7.5 kg each of nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium. At bud stage I add 15 kg urea per mu. Then at flowering I add another 15 kg urea and 25 kg potassium chloride per mu. The potassium chloride gives about 13 kg potassium. So total per mu is about 21 kg nitrogen, 7.5 kg phosphorus, and 20 kg potassium. Twenty years ago I saw that if cotton does not get enough potassium, the bolls fall off, so I do not cut corners there. I water three times—at bud, at full flower, and at boll. I spray pesticide four times because even with Bt seed, aphids and spider mites still attack every year. I expect 280 kg of seed cotton per mu. Last year I got 260 kg, so 280 should be reachable if I feed it well.

I think about money as one pot. I will spend a bit more on fertilizer this year because grain and cotton prices are decent, but I am not buying new machinery. I keep the cotton at 5.5 mu because picking by hand in autumn is hard work. The wheat and maize give steady grain income, and cotton pays for daily costs. I use the well to water all three crops because rain alone is never enough here. If I am not sure about something, I do what I did last year. Change is risky when you are 64.
